title: Senegal head coach on AFCON dispute: ‘Everybody knows we are champions of Africa’
content:
Senegal coach Pape Thiaw said “everybody knows that we are champions of Africa” as his country’s appeal to reinstate their 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) title continues.

Thiaw’s side were stripped of their second AFCON and Morocco declared winners by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) after the coach encouraged his players to leave the pitch during January’s final in Rabat.

That followed a controversial decision to award Morocco a late penalty after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out. Brahim Diaz then missed the spot-kick after a 16-minute delay, in which Senegal eventually returned to the field.

Senegal went on to beat Morocco through an extra-time goal from Pape Gueye, but this month the result was reversed by African football’s governing body CAF and awarded as a 3-0 win to the side who were losing finalists — 57 days after that match.

Asked whether he still felt like a champion of Africa, Thiaw said: “I’m focused on my work. For me, the most important thing is to not be distracted. Everybody knows that we’re champions of Africa.

“We’re going to continue to work to try and claim other trophies. Because we’re clear in our heads that competitions are won on the pitch and that’s what we did. We’re champions of Africa.”

Speaking alongside Thiaw before Saturday’s friendly against Peru at the Stade de France in Paris, Everton and Senegal midfielder Idrissa Gueye added: “As players, nobody can replace the strong emotions we’ve experienced.

“It’s been four AFCONs, (in which Senegal have reached) a final and twice (been) champions of Africa, and we didn’t steal those results. It’s the work of a whole country, of a whole, serious nation who give everything on and off the pitch.

“We didn’t steal those results, we deserved them and we deserve to be champions of Africa on the pitch. We’re going to try to just do the same thing off the pitch, we’ll continue to fight.”

Ahead of the Senegal press conference, Peru coach Mano Menezes also spoke to the media and addressed the dispute. “We always prefer to respect what happens on the pitch,” he said. “For us, we’re going to face the champions of Africa.”

Thiaw, 45, was also asked what he now thought of his decision to take the players off the pitch against Morocco but instead chose to focus on his relationship with Senegal fans at home in his answer. At the time, the ex-Liverpool forward Sadio Mane was the only Senegalese player who stayed on the pitch, encouraging his team-mates to return.

Thiaw and Gueye were speaking against a backdrop that read “Champions d’Afrique” and carried two stars — representing Senegal’s maiden victory in 2021 and this year’s disputed title — before the game against Peru, at which Senegal are set to parade the AFCON trophy.

The Senegalese Football Federation has appealed the decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), with one of the lawyers representing Senegal telling a press conference this week “there is no decision today from CAF or its appeals jury that orders the Senegalese Football Federation or the national team to return their medals or to return the trophy on the pitch”.

On March 18, the Senegalese government called for an investigation into alleged corruption at African football’s governing body.
